stories.title: D11 Offers Free Literacy Program During Fall Break [T1 — NEW]

x_posts.label: Post 1
x_posts.text: D11 fall break starts Monday (Oct 19-23). New this year: a free, voluntary 3-day reading program for kindergarteners who could use extra support. Plus D49 break runs through Oct 23. What are your plans? #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Fall break starts tomorrow for D11 and D49 families, and if you have a kindergartener in D11 who's been working on reading skills, there's something worth knowing about. 📚

The Gazette reported this weekend that District 11 is offering a voluntary, free three-day literacy program during fall break for kindergarteners who could use some extra support. It's not mandatory, and it's designed to give younger readers a little boost in a low-pressure setting. The district hasn't made a big announcement about it, so this might be news to some families.

Meanwhile, D49's fall break runs through October 23 — that's two full weeks off. And D20 already had its "end of quarter break" following parent-teacher conferences last week.

If you have a kindergartener in D11 and you're interested in the literacy program, reach out to your school directly for details on timing and how to sign up.

What are you doing with your kids during fall break this year?

article.headline: D11 Is Offering Free Reading Support for Kindergarteners During Fall Break

stories.title: Primark 101 Dalmatians Coin Purse Recalled for Phthalate Hazard [T1 — NEW]

x_posts.label: Post 2
x_posts.text: RECALL: Primark 101 Dalmatians coin purses (Oct 15, CPSC). About 2,100 units contain phthalates — a chemical risk for young children. Model #2595301 on the zip tag. Return to any Primark store for a full refund. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Heads up, Colorado Springs parents — if you picked up a 101 Dalmatians coin purse from Primark in the last several months, you'll want to check it. 🚨

The Consumer Product Safety Commission announced a recall on October 15 for about 2,100 Primark 101 Dalmatians faux-leather coin purses. The issue is phthalates — chemicals found at levels above what's permitted, which can be harmful to young children through ingestion. The purses were sold at Primark stores in the Northeast, Florida, Maryland, and Illinois from March through June 2026 for about $9.

Here's how to identify the recalled item: the model number 2595301 is on the tag attached to the zip puller. If it matches, stop letting kids use it and return it to any Primark store for a full refund. The CPSC says no injuries have been reported, but the risk is real.

The same purse was recalled in the UK back in September, so this has been on the radar for a while.

Did you have this item in your home?

article.headline: CPSC Recalls Primark 101 Dalmatians Coin Purses Over Phthalate Hazard

stories.title: Xalirium Portable Bed Rails Recalled for Entrapment Risk [T2 — NEW]

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text: RECALL: usOpal Xalirium portable bed rails (Oct 15, CPSC). About 200 units. Entrapment and asphyxiation risk — fails federal safety standard. Sold on Amazon Feb-Aug 2026 for ~$60. Stop use, contact usOpal for a refund. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Another CPSC recall from October 15 that families should know about — especially if grandparents or other caregivers use portable bed rails at home. 🛏️

The CPSC recalled about 200 usOpal Xalirium portable bed rails due to entrapment and asphyxiation risk. The rails fail the federal mandatory safety standard for adult portable bed rails and they're missing required hazard warning labels. They were sold on Amazon from February through August 2026 for around $60.

The recall is specifically for bed rails without vertical bars inside the opening — that's the detail to check. If you have them, stop using them and contact usOpal for a full refund. No injuries have been reported.

These might be in your home if you have elderly parents, grandparents visiting, or anyone using a bed rail for nighttime safety. Worth a quick check.

Is this something your family uses?

article.headline: CPSC Recalls Xalirium Portable Bed Rails for Entrapment and Asphyxiation Risk

stories.title: Halloween Week in COS — Events and Activities for Families [T2 — NEW]

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text: Halloween week in Colorado Springs: Boo at the Zoo runs through October (~$19.75-$24.75). Fiddler on the Roof at First Company Theatre through Nov 1 (family-friendly). More trunk-or-treats coming all week. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Fall break starts Monday, and Halloween is 13 days away. COS has a solid lineup of events to keep families busy this week and next. 🎃

Boo at the Zoo at Cheyenne Mountain Zoo runs through October — tickets are roughly $19.75-$24.75 per person. It's one of the region's most popular family events, and it books up, so check availability before you plan around it.

Fiddler on the Roof is playing at First Company Theatre (420 N Nevada Ave) through November 1. It's a great pick for older kids and a genuinely fun night out for the whole family.

Community trunk-or-treats, harvest festivals, and fall fairs will be popping up throughout the week. Keep an eye on local church and neighborhood Facebook groups — those events often don't get big advertising pushes but show up in community feeds.

What's your Halloween plan this year — big event or neighborhood trick-or-treat?

article.headline: Halloween Week in Colorado Springs: What to Do with Kids This Fall Break

stories.title: How COS School Districts Are Embracing Fall Breaks [T2 — NEW]

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text: D11 (Oct 19-23), D49 (Oct 13-23), D20 (end-of-quarter break): COS school districts have embraced fall breaks. The Gazette looked at why — and what the tradeoffs are for families and the school calendar. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Colorado Springs families have noticed: fall break is getting bigger across our school districts.

The Gazette published a piece this weekend looking at how D11, D49, and D20 have each developed their own version of fall break. D11's one-week break (Oct 19-23) is the most recent addition — the district has even added a free literacy program this year for kindergarteners who want extra reading support. D49 runs two full weeks off, which means a longer overall school year to compensate. D20 structured its break around parent-teacher conferences, calling it an "end of quarter" break.

The community response has generally been positive. Parents like having a mid-fall recharge, and the Gazette notes that general consensus is the schedule should stay as it is. There's a real argument that the pace of modern school calendars benefits from a mid-fall pause — and COS districts seem to agree.

It's worth knowing your district's specific schedule and planning accordingly. D49 families still have several days of break remaining. D11 families start theirs tomorrow.

How do you feel about fall break in COS — is the schedule working for your family?

article.headline: COS School Districts Have Embraced Fall Breaks — Here's What to Know
